facts.claim: The hippocampus may not be needed for the storage and recovery of a spatial layout that was experienced long before injury.
facts.quote: there is now evidence that the hippocampus may not be needed for the storage and recovery of a spatial layout that was experienced long before injury.

facts.claim: Right medial temporal lobe activity was observed during navigation tasks, but the core of the activated region was in the parahippocampal gyrus, barely touching the hippocampus proper.
facts.quote: Importantly, right medial temporal lobe activity was observed, its magnitude equivalent across all tasks, though the core of the activated region was in the parahippocampal gyrus, barely touching the hippocampus proper.

facts.claim: The retrosplenial cortex allows the combination of idiothetic cues, spatial relations, and environmental features into a spatial map that can dynamically support goal-directed navigation.
facts.quote: We argue that the integrative properties of RC allow the combination of idiothetic cues, spatial relations (allocentric and egocentric), and environmental features (landmarks, boundaries, etc.) into a spatial map that can dynamically support goal-directed navigation.

facts.claim: Only 0.8% of the neuroarchitecture corpus has reached Stage IV (Adaptive Design Operationalization).
facts.quote: only 0. 8% reached Stage IV (Adaptive Design Operationalization).

facts.claim: Spatial memory declines with age, but the relevance of different landmark cues for specifying heading directions among different age groups has not been clarified.
facts.quote: Previous studies have showed that spatial memory declines with age but have not clarified the relevance of different landmark cues for specifying heading directions among different age groups.

research.angle: While the hippocampus may not be necessary for long-term spatial memory storage, the retrosplenial cortex integrates environmental features like landmarks into dynamic maps for navigation.
research.verdict: The sources do not provide evidence that modern cities atrophy the hippocampus; instead, they suggest the hippocampus might not be required for long-term spatial storage and highlight other brain structures involved in navigation.
research.caveat: The sources lack specific data on how modern urban design specifically impacts the rate of hippocampal atrophy or spatial memory decline.
